transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes. Quick roll call - Lina?
[00:06] Lina: Here, hi.
[00:08] Owen: here.
[00:09] Sara: yep, hi all.
[00:12] Maya: Cool. Diego's going to run through the cost numbers we promised from the test last week. Diego, over to you.
[00:20] Diego: Thanks. So quick context, we ran three main configs: baseline (hosted, no caching, small batch), batching heavy (batch=128, delayed 25ms), and caching enabled (prefix+KV cache). Results are on the spreadsheet link.
[00:35] Diego: Baseline throughput was about 1.2k tokens/sec per dollar (we're using our internal tokens/sec/$ metric), with p95 latency ~140ms on the 2k token sequence test. When we enable batching aggressively we see throughput improve to ~2.1k tokens/sec/$ but p95 latency jumps to ~280-320ms depending on tail.
[00:56] Lina: OK, that matches what we feared — more tokens per dollar but latency doubles. Our SLA for inference needs 200ms p95, so big batching might breach that.
[01:06] Diego: Right, that's the tradeoff. But with KV cache enabled we reduced token generation by about 28% on repeated prompts (similar prefix reuse) which translates to ~35% cost savings in that workload — effectively moving baseline tokens/sec/$ from 1.2k to ~1.6k.
[01:25] Owen: Wait, 28% fewer tokens — is that simulated or from live traffic?
[01:28] Diego: This was measured with the sample trace you shared last week — we replayed two days of traffic and measured repeated prefix reuse. We also estimated worst-case and best-case ranges.
[01:38] Sara: Any impact on memory or GPU footprint with KV cache? We're worried about eviction thrash.
[01:42] Diego: Good question — KV cache increases GPU memory usage for the key-values keyed per session. At our settings the extra memory is about 6-8% on a p4d-equivalent instance. If you pin sessions to specific GPUs (sticky routing) eviction is minimal. We can tune TTLs for older sessions.
[01:56] Lina: And what about quantization? If we use int8_quant we lose some quality but improve throughput, right?
[02:01] Diego: Yes, quantization to int8 improved tokens/sec/$ by ~20% in our synthetic runs. Quality drop is model-dependent; we recommend running evals on your golden prompts. We can include quantization variants in the next benchmark.
[02:14] Maya: Quick pause — Owen, you mentioned on the repo you care about 99th percentile latency for interactive editors. Is that still the case?
[02:19] Owen: Yes, editors need <250ms for 99th ideally, 200ms p95. So any config that pushes 99th >350ms is a non-starter.
[02:27] Diego: Understood. So summary: batching helps cost but hurts tail latencies; KV cache gives substantive token savings without huge latency impact; quantization gives throughput wins but must be validated for quality.
[02:37] Lina: Could you show the per-route breakdown? Some routes are chat-like with lots of repetition, which will get great benefit from caching; others are open-ended generation where batching helps more.
[02:48] Diego: Yep — on the spreadsheet we added route-by-route tokens saved: chat_routes saw ~45% repeated token savings; completion_routes only ~10%. That suggests we should enable aggressive KV cache for chat endpoints and selectively batch completions.
[03:02] Maya: Are there any cost examples that map to your current billing? Like if Quantaco moves 1M monthly queries what does that look like hosted vs dedicated?
[03:10] Diego: We made a quick scenario: Hosted baseline cost per month at current profile is roughly $14k for 1M queries. With KV cache and selective batching that drops to about $9k. Dedicated (reserved) with similar utilization and autoscale would be approx $7k/mo but requires a monthly commit and has a higher upfront. These are rough — we'll send exact numbers in the cost model.
[03:28] Owen: What's assumed in the dedicated estimate — instance size, utilization?
[03:31] Diego: We assumed an 8xA10 or comparable cluster with 70% utilization, and plus reserved discount. If you want lower latency SLOs we can change the instance mix.
[03:42] Sara: On the dedicated option — how does model pinning work? We can't have auto-fallback to a lower quality model for legal reasons.
[03:48] Diego: In Redwood Dedicated you can pin model versions and disable fallback. In hosted mode by default we have a model catalog with fallbacks but we can opt out for enterprise customers and lock routing policies.
[03:58] Lina: Back to cost/unit — what's tokens/sec/$ definition again? I want to be clear how you compute across mixed load.
[04:04] Diego: It's tokens processed per second divided by cost per second for the fleet, normalized; basically throughput per dollar. For mixed load we weight by observed route distribution — that's why we asked for that CSV.
[04:15] Owen: That makes sense. One more: if we enable both caching and batching do the benefits stack linearly?
[04:21] Diego: Not perfectly. Caching reduces the tokens that need generation, which reduces how much batching can help. In our runs caching+moderate-batching gave the best practical sweet spot: tokens/sec/$ ~2.0k with p95 ~180-210ms. Aggressive batching after caching had diminishing returns and pushed p95 above SLA.
[04:40] Lina: Any gotchas on KV cache warm up in early hours? We have bursty traffic first thing in the morning.
[04:45] Diego: Yes cold-start reduces cache hits. We suggest small warm pools and a short TTL for night sessions. Also pre-warming common prefixes if you have scheduled jobs helps.
[04:53] Owen: For the benchmark you plan to run, what's the load profile? Will it emulate bursts?
[04:57] Diego: We'll replay the actual two-day trace you gave and run a separate bursty test to emulate morning spikes. We'll capture tails and compute cost metrics.
[05:04] Sara: Security question quick — does KV cache persist encrypted at rest?
[05:08] Diego: For hosted the cached KV is ephemeral in memory on the GPU nodes; for Dedicated we can offer encrypted cache persistence and KMS integration. We'll document this in the security packet.
[05:18] Maya: Good. Any blockers from the Quantaco side to run this next benchmark?
[05:22] Owen: We'll share the additional sample traffic and can whitelist IPs for the test. Also Lina will surface a few golden prompts for quality checks.
[05:29] Lina: I'll get those by EOD Tuesday.
[05:31] Maya: Perfect. Quick recap of action items...
[05:34] Maya: Diego to run KV-cache-enabled benchmark and send logs + cost outputs by 2025-09-08. Maya to send updated cost model with tokens/sec/$ and scenario pricing by 2025-09-05. Owen to share expanded traffic + whitelist info by 2025-09-07.
[05:48] Sara: Sounds good.
[05:50] Lina: Thanks all.
[05:51] Maya: Thanks — we'll reconvene next week same time to review results.
[05:54] [call ends]
